developer_response.body:
Dear wilz57,
Thank you for your interest in Samsung Internet. We are very sorry for causing you such inconvenience.
For checking your problem, could you send us log file for us?
[1] - Start "Samsung Internet VR" and reenact your update problem and eject your phone.
[2] - Select the 'Phone' icon on your galaxy device and dial *#9900#
[3] - Press "RUN DUMPSTATE/LOGCAT" ( Wait for a minute )
[4] - Press "COPY TO SDCARD(INCLUDE CP RAMDUMP)
[5] - Log file will be saved your device storage. You can check your log file in "/log" on your device storage.
Please send us your log file then we can check your problem. You can send us an email to browser@samsung.com.
After making log files, try to uninstall and reinstall "Samsung Internet VR" to solve the problem, temporarily.
(Go to "Setting" - "Applications" - "Samsung Internet VR" - "Uninstall" and try to reinstall "Samsung Internet VR" in Oculus Store) 
Feel free to reach out to us if you need further assistance.

Great update, make video more immersive

It's surprising that a browser that works only in VR requires you to flip a setting before it works with WebVR. It's in the "Labs" menu. (Without that, even Samsung WebVR demos don't work.)

Once you do that, it has good support for the current "WebVR 1.1" standard, even allowing you to navigate links in VR mode (which most VR browsers don't).

Unfortunately, performance (frame rates) is noticeably worse than the Oculus browser.

2D websites are rendered properly.

The on-screen keyboard is too small, and Gear VR appears to lack a way to copy URLs from the regular Android mode.

developer_response.body:
Hello. We are very sorry for causing you such inconvenience.

"internet://webvr-enable" has been deprecated.
You can turn on WebVR by following below steps.
If “Labs” menu in “More” is exposed,
1. Enter Labs
2. Toggle switch
3. Press back key
If not,
1. Fetch “internet://flags”
2. Select “Enable” for WebVR
3. Relaunch Samsung Internet for GearVR
Thank you for your interest in Samsung Internet.
